newsitem.title: USA: CBOT new crop soymeal closes lower, soyoil down.
newsitem.headline: CBOT new crop soymeal closes lower, soyoil down.

text.p: CBOT new crop soymeal futures ended sharply lower on surprisingly high USDA 1997 planted soybean acreage estimates but old crop closed higher on ideas of tight stocks, traders said.
Soyoil prices closed lower across the board.
USDA on Monday estimated 1997 soybean plantings at 68.8 million acres, the highest since 1980 and well above trade expectations for 65.85 million.
But old crop contracts held firm on ideas lower-than- expected quarterly stocks figures would lead to dangerously tight ending stocks.

"The market seemed to react more toward the prospects of very large supplies come fall than the very strong demand pace evidenced by the stocks figure," said Joel Karlin, analyst with Everen Securities in Chicago.

"We're talking about exceptionally large, perhaps record corn and soybean crops," he added. "But demand for U.S. beans continues to be very strong. Even at these prices, it does not appear to have stifled even domestic demand."
Soymeal closed $7.50 per ton lower to $0.30 higher with May up $0.30 at $283.00 a ton. Soyoil closed 0.65 to 0.30 cent per lb lower with May down 0.50 at 23.92 cents.
